review_notes: Read the whole file. Its proofs use only `simp only [Category.assoc]` and `rw`, so its own simp usage is clean. I found no cycles or competing rules. The one concrete simp-interface problem is the `attribute [-simp]` on line 11, which works around a globally registered `@[simp]` lemma defined elsewhere. The grep count for that line (799 files) was capped by head_limit=5, so 799 is the total over matching files. I did not check which of those files actually call plain `simp` and are affected. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour.

findings.declaration: attribute [-simp] RegularLocalRingQuotientAscent.dualNumberFst_apply (file-level workaround for a globally @[simp] lemma)
findings.problem: The lemma `dualNumberFst_apply` is declared `@[simp]` in an imported Definitions file. It rewrites `dualNumberFst K x` to `TrivSqZeroExt.fst x`, which unfolds the named ring hom into its underlying function. This file has to switch the lemma off. The grep for this exact line returned a count of 799 across 799 files, so the pattern is copied into every downstream file instead of being fixed at the source. The simp set exposed to importers is therefore poorly designed: the rule expands a definition by default and every client must opt out. In this file the line is dead anyway, since the proofs only use `simp only [Category.assoc]` and `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: In Definitions/Def_AlgebraicGeometry_RegularLocalRingQuotientNonZeroDivisorAscent.lean, drop `@[simp]` from `dualNumberFst_apply` (or make it a `local simp` or scoped attribute). The only in-file use found is an explicit `rw [... dualNumberFst_apply]`, which needs no simp attribute. Then delete the `attribute [-simp] ...` line here and in the other files that copy it. Downstream files that actually rely on the rewrite can call `simp [RegularLocalRingQuotientAscent.dualNumberFst_apply]`.
findings.benefit: Importers get a default simp set that does not unfold `dualNumberFst`. About 800 boilerplate lines disappear, and nobody has to remember the workaround in new files.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp] theorem dualNumberFst_apply (K : Type*) [CommRing K] (x : DualNumber K) :
    dualNumberFst K x = TrivSqZeroExt.fst x := rfl
